et omnem animam viventem atque* motabile: and every living and moving creature, which the waters brought forth, according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind.

bestias terre iuxta species suas et iume: the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and cattle,

et cunctis animantibus terre omnique vol: And to all beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so done.

celi et terre quando create sunt in die: of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day

hominem de limo terre: man of the slime of the earth:
in faciem eius spiraculum vite: into his face the breath of life,
and man became a living soul.

wherein he placed man whom he had formed.
Produxitque Dominus Deus de humo omne li: And the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold,
et ad vescendum suave, lignum etiam vite: and pleasant to eat of: the tree of life also
LIGNUMQUE SCIENTIE BONI ET MALI: and the tree of knowledge of good and evil
qui inde dividitur in quatuor: which from thence is divided into four
Nomen uni Phison,: The name of the one is Phison:

the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia.

the same passeth along by the Assyrians.
fluvius autem quartus ipse est Euphrates: And the fourth river is Euphrates.

scientie boni et mali: of knowledge of good and evil,
